How to use this

This is a condensed reference. Each bullet = a high-yield point for SSC. Use this on the day before the exam. For depth, click into the relevant chapter.

---

A. National Symbols (from 14 - National Symbols of India)

  • Flag: Tiranga, 3:2 ratio, designed by Pingali Venkayya.
  • Emblem: Lion Capital of Ashoka (Sarnath), adopted 26 Jan 1950. "Satyameva Jayate" — Mundaka Upanishad.
  • Anthem: Jana Gana Mana — Tagore (Bengali), adopted 24 Jan 1950. Plays in 52 sec.
  • Song: Vande Mataram — Bankim Chandra, Anandamath (1882).
  • Animal: Royal Bengal Tiger (1973).
  • Bird: Indian Peacock (1963).
  • Flower: Lotus.
  • Tree: Banyan.
  • Fruit: Mango; Vegetable: Pumpkin (2021).
  • River: Ganga (2008).
  • Game: No official national game.
  • Reptile: King Cobra (2021).
  • Aquatic animal: Gangetic Dolphin (2011).
  • Heritage animal: Indian Elephant (2010).
  • Calendar: Saka Calendar (Chaitra 1 = 22 March, 1957).
  • Pledge: "India is my country…" — written by Pydimarri Venkata Subba Rao (Telugu).

B. First in India (from 15 - First in India and World)

  • First President: Dr. Rajendra Prasad.
  • First VP: Dr. S. Radhakrishnan.
  • First PM: Jawaharlal Nehru.
  • First Home Minister: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel.
  • First Speaker (LS): G.V. Mavalankar.
  • First woman PM: Indira Gandhi.
  • First woman Speaker: Meira Kumar.
  • First woman CM: Sucheta Kripalani (UP).
  • First woman Governor: Sarojini Naidu (UP).
  • First woman President UNGA: Vijaya Lakshmi Pandit (1953).
  • First woman to receive Bharat Ratna: Indira Gandhi.
  • First woman to receive Nobel (Indian-born): Mother Teresa (1979).
  • First in space: Rakesh Sharma (1984).
  • First Indian Olympic gold (individual): Abhinav Bindra (2008).
  • First Cricket test match: 1877 (Australia vs England).
  • First ODI: 1971 (Australia vs England, Melbourne).
  • First ODI for India: 1971 (vs England).
  • First Test for India: 1932.
  • First Census of India: 1872 (Lord Mayo); First synchronous: 1881 (Lord Ripon, W.C. Plowden).
  • First Newspaper: Hicky's Bengal Gazette (1780).
  • First Indian film: Raja Harishchandra (1913) — Dadasaheb Phalke.
  • First sound film: Alam Ara (1931) — Ardeshir Irani.
  • First Indian to win Oscar: Bhanu Athaiya (1983).
  • First Honorary Oscar: Satyajit Ray (1992).
  • First train: 1853 (Mumbai–Thane).
  • First metro: Kolkata (1984).
  • First atomic power station: Tarapur (1969).
  • First satellite: Aryabhata (1975, by USSR).
  • First missile: Prithvi (1988).
  • First supercomputer: PARAM 8000 (1991, C-DAC).
  • First nuclear test: Smiling Buddha (Pokhran-I, 1974).
  • First H-bomb test: Pokhran-II (1998).
  • First woman IAS: Anna Rajam George (1951).
  • First woman IPS: Kiran Bedi (1972).
  • First woman Chief Election Commissioner: V.S. Ramadevi (1990).
  • First Jnanpith winner: G. Sankara Kurup (1965).
  • First woman Jnanpith: Ashapoorna Devi (1976).
  • First ever field hockey team in Olympics (India, gold): 1928 Amsterdam (Captain: Jaipal Singh Munda).

C. First in World

  • First vaccine: Edward Jenner (smallpox, 1796).
  • First antibiotic: Alexander Fleming (Penicillin, 1928).
  • First person in space: Yuri Gagarin (1961).
  • First woman in space: Valentina Tereshkova (1963).
  • First man on Moon: Neil Armstrong (1969).
  • First satellite: Sputnik-1 (USSR, 1957).
  • First living being in space: Laika (dog, 1957).
  • First to climb Everest: Tenzing Norgay + Edmund Hillary (1953).
  • First to South Pole: Roald Amundsen (1911).
  • First to North Pole: Robert Peary (claimed 1909).
  • First to circumnavigate: Magellan's expedition (1522).
  • First solo circumnavigation: Joshua Slocum (1895–98).
  • First flight across Atlantic (non-stop): Alcock and Brown (1919).
  • First solo non-stop Atlantic: Charles Lindbergh (1927).
  • First heart transplant: Christiaan Barnard (1967, S. Africa).
  • First test-tube baby: Louise Brown (1978, UK).
  • First website: Tim Berners-Lee (CERN, 1991).
  • First person to win 2 Nobels: Marie Curie (1903, 1911).
  • First country to give women the right to vote: New Zealand (1893).
  • First country to use paper money: China (Tang Dynasty, 7th c).
  • First country to grant written constitution: USA (1787).
  • First country to abolish slavery: France (1794) — modern: Haiti (1804) / UK (1833).
  • First Asian to win Nobel: Rabindranath Tagore (1913, Literature).
  • First Indian to win Nobel in Physics: C.V. Raman (1930).
  • First Indian to win Nobel in Medicine/Physiology: — (no Indian)
  • First Indian to win Nobel in Economics: Amartya Sen (1998).

  • Capital of Nigeria: Abuja (not Lagos).

  • Capital of USA: Washington, D.C. (not New York).
  • Capital of Vietnam: Hanoi (not Ho Chi Minh).
  • Currency of Japan: Yen.
  • Currency of UK: Pound Sterling (GBP).
  • Currency of China: Renminbi (CNY).
  • Currency of Brazil: Real.
  • Currency of Iran: Rial.
  • Currency of Saudi Arabia: Saudi Riyal.
  • Currency of UAE: Dirham.
  • Currency of Pakistan: PKR; Bangladesh: Taka; Sri Lanka: LKR.

E. Boundary Lines (from 17 - Boundary Lines of India)

  • Radcliffe Line: India–Pakistan, Cyril Radcliffe, 1947. Also India–East Pakistan (now Bangladesh).
  • McMahon Line: India–China, McMahon, 1914 (Simla Convention). China doesn't recognise.
  • Durand Line: Afghanistan–Pakistan, 1893. Afghanistan doesn't recognise.
  • LoC: India–Pakistan in J&K and Ladakh, 1971 ceasefire, 740 km.
  • LAC: India–China, de facto, 3,488 km, 3 sectors (Western, Middle, Eastern).
  • Hindu Line: Inside Pakistan, 1965 war, India drew.
  • 17th Parallel: India–Myanmar (older Pemberton Line).
  • 38th Parallel: North–South Korea.
  • Indira Point: Southernmost of India (Andaman).
  • Indira Col: Northernmost of India (Ladakh).
  • Kanyakumari: Southernmost of mainland.
  • Attari–Wagah: India–Pakistan, Punjab; beating retreat.
  • Sir Creek: India–Pakistan, Gujarat–Sindh.
  • India's 7 land neighbours: Pakistan, China, Nepal, Bhutan, Bangladesh, Myanmar, Afghanistan (via PoK).
  • Longest border: Bangladesh (4,096 km).
  • Open border: Nepal; Bhutan.
  • Palk Strait: between India and Sri Lanka.
  • 10° Channel: Andaman–Nicobar; 9° Channel: Lakshadweep–Minicoy; 8° Channel: Maldives–Minicoy.

F. UNESCO WHS (from 18 - UNESCO World Heritage Sites in India)

  • India: 43 WHS (35 cultural + 7 natural + 1 mixed) as of 2025.
  • First WHS (1983): Agra Fort, Ajanta Caves, Ellora Caves, Taj Mahal.
  • First mixed WHS: Khangchendzonga NP (2016).
  • First natural WHS: Kaziranga NP (1985).
  • 2024 additions: Maratha Military Landscapes, Moidams of Charaideo.
  • Intangible heritage (14 entries): Kutiyattam, Vedic chanting, Ramlila, Mudiyettu, Kalbelia, Chhau dance, Buddhist chanting, Sankirtana, Thatheras, Yoga, Kumbh Mela, Durga Puja, Garba, Panchang.
  • Kaziranga = Indian one-horned rhinoceros.
  • Sundarbans = largest mangrove, Royal Bengal Tiger.
  • Nalanda = ancient university (2016).
  • Dholavira = Harappan site (2021).
  • Sacred Ensembles of Hoysala (2023).

  • Polio (oral): Sabin; (injection): Salk.

I. Temples & Pilgrimage (from 21 - Important Temples and Pilgrimage Sites)

  • 12 Jyotirlingas: Somnath, Mallikarjuna (Srisailam), Mahakaleshwar (Ujjain), Omkareshwar, Vaidyanath (Deoghar), Bhimashankar, Ramanathaswamy (Rameshwaram), Nageshwar (Dwarka), Vishwanath (Kashi), Tryambakeshwar (Nashik), Kedarnath, Grishneshwar.
  • Char Dham (Vishnu): Puri, Dwarka, Badrinath, Rameshwaram.
  • Char Dham (Himalayan): Yamunotri, Gangotri, Kedarnath, Badrinath.
  • 4 Mathas (Adi Shankara): Sringeri (South), Dwaraka (West), Jyotir (North), Govardhan (East).
  • Sapta Puri (7 holy cities): Ayodhya, Mathura, Haridwar, Varanasi, Kanchi, Ujjain, Dwarka.
  • Vaishno Devi: J&K, Trikuta mountains.
  • Golden Temple (Harmandir Sahib): Amritsar, Punjab.
  • Tirumala Tirupati (Balaji): Andhra Pradesh — richest temple.
  • Sabarimala: Kerala (restricted entry).

J. Committees & Reports (from 22 - Important Committees and Reports)

  • Drafting Committee (Constitution): B.R. Ambedkar.
  • President of Constituent Assembly: V.N. Pattabhi Sitaramayya (later Dr. Rajendra Prasad).
  • Sarkaria Commission: Centre-State (1983, R.S. Sarkaria).
  • Punchhi Commission: Centre-State (2007–10, M.M. Punchhi).
  • Kothari Commission: Education (1964–66, D.S. Kothari).
  • Balwant Rai Mehta: Panchayati Raj (1957).
  • Ashok Mehta: Panchayati Raj (1977).
  • Tendulkar Committee: Poverty (2009).
  • Rangarajan Committee: Poverty (2014).
  • Santhanam Committee: Anti-corruption → Lokayukta (1962).
  • Vohra Committee: Criminalisation of politics (1993).
  • Narasimham Committee: Banking reforms (1991, 1998).
  • Fazal Ali Commission (SRC): Linguistic reorganisation (1953).
  • T.S.R. Subramanian: UPSC reform (2014).
  • Swaran Singh: Punjab reorganisation (1976).
  • Shah Commission: Assam-Nagaland (1966).
  • Mahajan Commission: Karnataka-Maharashtra (1967).
  • States Reorganisation Act: 1956 (based on Fazal Ali).
  • NEP 2020: K. Kasturirangan.
  • National Education Policy 1968: Kothari-led.
  • NPE 1986: Rajiv Gandhi era; later modified as NEP 2020.

  • Lowest population density: Arunachal Pradesh (17/km²).

  • Capital of Andhra Pradesh: Amaravati.
  • Capital of Telangana: Hyderabad.
  • Capital of Gujarat: Gandhinagar.
  • Capital of Maharashtra: Mumbai.
  • State with most Lok Sabha seats: UP (80).
  • State with most Rajya Sabha seats: UP (31).
  • J&K and Ladakh are UTs (since 31 Oct 2019).

M. Battles (from 24 - Important Battles in Indian History)

  • First Tarain (1191): Prithviraj Chauhan won.
  • Second Tarain (1192): Muhammad Ghori won.
  • First Panipat (1526): Babur defeated Lodi.
  • Khanwa (1527): Babur vs Rana Sanga.
  • Chanderi (1528): Babur vs Medini Ray.
  • Haldighati (1576): Man Singh (Mughal) won; Rana Pratap's horse Chetak died.
  • Second Panipat (1556): Akbar (Bairam Khan) defeated Hemu.
  • Third Panipat (1761): Abdali defeated Marathas.
  • Plassey (1757): Clive defeated Siraj-ud-Daulah.
  • Buxar (1764): British defeated Mir Qasim, Shuja-ud-Daula, Shah Alam II.
  • Kalinga (261 BC): Ashoka defeated Kalinga; converted to Buddhism.
  • Saraighat (1671): Ahoms (Lachit Borphukan) defeated Mughals.
  • Waterloo (1815): Wellington + Blücher defeated Napoleon.

N. Frequently-confused pairs (memorize these)

  • Bharat vs India: Constitution says "India, that is Bharat" (Article 1).
  • Solidiers: Last Guru Gobind Singh: at Nanded (Hazoor Sahib).
  • First PM of UK: Robert Walpole.
  • First President of USA: George Washington.
  • First woman President of India: Pratibha Patil (2007).
  • First woman PM of India: Indira Gandhi.
  • First woman in Indian Army combat: Captain Lakshmi Sahgal (1943, Rani of Jhansi Regiment).
  • First Dalit Chief Justice of India: K.G. Balakrishnan.
  • First Muslim President of INC: Badruddin Tyabji.
  • First woman to scale Mt. Everest (Indian): Bachendri Pal (1984).
  • First Asian to climb Everest: Tenzing Norgay (1953, with Hillary).
  • First solo Everest (Indians): Malavath Purna (2014) — youngest Indian to climb Everest.

  • Number of Indian states: 28.

  • World's highest waterfall: Angel Falls (Venezuela).

  • World's smallest country (by area): Vatican City.

P. High-yield Mnemonics (SSC-proven)

  • G7 countries (BF JUICE): Britain, France, Japan, USA, Italy, Canada, Germany, EU.
  • SAARC countries (BIMUN PM C): Bangladesh, India, Maldives, (then 6 others) — note: 8 members.
  • G20 (19 countries + EU + AU): Argentina, Australia, Brazil, Canada, China, France, Germany, India, Indonesia, Italy, Japan, Mexico, South Korea, Russia, Saudi Arabia, South Africa, Turkey, UK, USA, EU, AU.
  • NATO members (32, 2024): 30 + Finland (2023) + Sweden (2024).
  • BRICS (now 10): Brazil, Russia, India, China, South Africa, + Iran, Egypt, Ethiopia, UAE, Saudi Arabia.
  • 4 Dhams (Vishnu): Puri, Dwarka, Badrinath, Rameshwaram — PDBR.
  • 4 Mathas (Shankara): Sringeri (S), Dwaraka (W), Jyotir (N), Govardhan (E) — S-D-J-G.
  • 7 Sapta Puri: Ayodhya, Mathura, Haridwar, Varanasi, Kanchi, Ujjain, Dwarka.
  • Census first synchronous: 1881 (Lord Ripon, W.C. Plowden).
  • Bharat Ratna first (1954): C. Rajagopalachari, S. Radhakrishnan, C.V. Raman.

Q. Top 30 One-Liners (1-line answers for 1-mark questions)

  1. 1. Longest river in India: Ganga.
  2. 2. Highest peak in India: Kangchenjunga (K2 is in PoK; Kangchenjunga is in Sikkim).
  3. 3. Highest peak in the world: Mt. Everest.
  4. 4. Largest lake in India: Wular Lake (J&K) — freshwater; Chilika Lake (Odisha) is largest brackish water lake.
  5. 5. Largest saltwater lake in India: Chilika (also the largest brackish lagoon in India).
  6. 6. Longest canal in India: Indira Gandhi Canal (Rajasthan).
  7. 7. Longest dam in India: Hirakud Dam (Odisha).
  8. 8. Longest river of South India: Godavari.
  9. 9. Largest delta in India: Sundarbans (Ganges–Brahmaputra).
  10. 10. Largest desert in India: Thar (Rajasthan).
  11. 11. Largest state by area: Rajasthan.
  12. 12. Smallest state by area: Goa.
  13. 13. Largest state by population: UP.
  14. 14. Smallest state by population: Sikkim.
  15. 15. National Game of India: No official national game.
  16. 16. National Tree of India: Banyan.
  17. 17. National Bird of India: Peacock.
  18. 18. National Animal of India: Bengal Tiger.
  19. 19. National River of India: Ganga.
  20. 20. Currency of India: Indian Rupee.
  21. 21. Largest Union Territory by area: Ladakh.
  22. 22. Smallest Union Territory by area: Lakshadweep.
  23. 23. Capital of India: New Delhi.
  24. 24. Lok Sabha seat of India: 543 elected + 2 nominated (Anglo-Indian, abolished by 104th Amendment in 2019). Now 543.
  25. 25. Rajya Sabha seat of India: 238 + 12 nominated.
  26. 26. Supreme Court of India: New Delhi; established 26 Jan 1950.
  27. 27. First President of India: Dr. Rajendra Prasad.
  28. 28. First Vice President of India: Dr. S. Radhakrishnan.
  29. 29. First PM of India: Jawaharlal Nehru.
  30. 30. First Home Minister: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel.

R. Mega-recap — what to revise the night before the exam

  1. 1. National Symbols (12 items) — 1 min review.
  2. 2. First in India (50+ items) — 5 min review.
  3. 3. Boundary lines (5–6 lines) — 2 min review.
  4. 4. Important Days (1 for each day of the year) — 3 min review.
  5. 5. Capitals & Currencies (top 50 countries) — 5 min review.
  6. 6. UNESCO WHS in India (top 10) — 2 min review.
  7. 7. Awards & Honours (top 15) — 3 min review.
  8. 8. Sports trophies & tournaments (top 20) — 3 min review.
  9. 9. Books & Authors (top 30) — 5 min review.
  10. 10. Indian States — capital + CM + Governor (all 28 + 8 UTs) — 10 min review.

Total: ~40 minutes for one solid revision of Static GK.

2024–2025 Updates (one-liner recap)

  • Bharat Ratna 2024: Karpoori Thakur, M.S. Swaminathan, P.V. Narasimha Rao, L.K. Advani, Chaudhary Charan Singh (all posthumous except L.K. Advani). India's 49 total recipients.
  • Padma Vibhushan 2025: D. Nageshwar Reddy, Jagdish Singh Khehar, Kumudini Rajnikant Lakhia, Lakshminarayana Subramaniam (verify Bindeshwar Pathak posthumous).
  • 58th Jnanpith (2024): Vinod Kumar Shukla, Jagadguru Rambhadracharya.
  • Dadasaheb Phalke 2024: Mithun Chakraborty.
  • 70th NFA (Best Film, 2024): Aattam.
  • Khel Ratna 2024: Gukesh D, Harmanpreet Singh, Praveen Kumar, Manu Bhaker.
  • UNESCO WHS count: 43 (after Maratha Military Landscapes + Moidams of Charaideo added in 2024).
  • UNESCO ICH 15th entry: Garba of Gujarat (2023).
  • Indian state elections 2024: AP → Chandrababu Naidu (TDP), Odisha → Mohan Charan Majhi (BJP, 1st BJP CM), Haryana → Nayab Singh Saini (BJP), Jharkhand → Hemant Soren (JMM, 4th time), Maharashtra → Devendra Fadnavis (BJP, Mahayuti).
  • Delhi elections Feb 2025: BJP won (first time since 1998); verify CM name.
  • Census 2021: delayed; expected in 2025–26.
  • Operation Sindoor (May 2025): India's post-Pahalgam response; targets in PoK and Pakistan.
  • One Nation, One Election: Kovind Committee report (2024) supports; bills in Parliament.
  • PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana (Feb 2024): rooftop solar for 1 crore households.
  • PM Internship Scheme (2024): 1 lakh youth, top 500 companies.
  • Vande Bharat Sleeper (2024): India's first indigenous semi-high-speed sleeper.
  • BRICS expansion (2024): 5 → 10 members (added Iran, Egypt, Ethiopia, UAE, Saudi Arabia [negotiating]).
  • Eurozone (2024): 20 members; Croatia joined Jan 2023.
  • NATO (2024): 32 members; Finland (2023), Sweden (2024).
  • Nobel 2024: Hopfield & Hinton (Physics, ML), Han Kang (Literature), Nihon Hidankyo (Peace).
  • Paris Olympics 2024 (India): 6 medals — Neeraj Chopra (silver), Manu Bhaker (2 bronze), Swapnil Kusale (bronze), Indian hockey (bronze), Aman Sehrawat (bronze).
For the day before the exam, lock in the 5 Bharat Ratna 2024 names, Padma Vibhushan 2025 (4 main names), 70th NFA Best Film = Aattam, Dadasaheb Phalke 2024 = Mithun Chakraborty, 58th Jnanpith (Vinod Kumar Shukla, Jagadguru Rambhadracharya), and the CMs of the 5 newly-elected states in 2024.
